title: Geometric-stalk test and inverse-image stability of Tor intervals
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $T$ a scheme, $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and $a\le b$ integers. Geometric stalks are as in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Then $K$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude] if and only if for every geometric point $\bar t$ and every $A$-module $M$ the complex $K_{\bar t}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$. Consequently for every scheme morphism $u:U\to T$, the exact constant-coefficient inverse image $u^*$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] preserves each Tor interval.

proof.text: Kernels and images of maps of module sheaves inherit the action of $A_T$, and their quotient has the induced action, so their underlying abelian sheaves compute the same kernels, images and cohomology. For any representing complex $C$ of $A_T$-module sheaves, apply exactness of geometric stalks to its underlying abelian sheaves. The exact-functor homology comparison, applied in degrees $i-1,i,i+1$, gives $H^i(C)_{\bar t}\cong H^i(C_{\bar t})$. In particular termwise stalks send quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms, so this identity is valid for every $E\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. A module sheaf is zero exactly when its underlying abelian sheaf is zero. Apply geometric-stalk conservativity to the map from that underlying abelian sheaf to zero: $H^i(E)=0$ if and only if $H^i(E_{\bar t})=0$ for every $\bar t$. This uses no bound on $E$.

Assume $K$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$. Fix a geometric point $\bar t$ and an arbitrary $A$-module $M$. In the defining quantifier for Tor amplitude take the degree-zero constant sheaf $\underline M$. Then $H^i(K\otimes_{A_T}^{\mathbf L}\underline M)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$. By step 1 the same vanishing holds after taking the stalk at $\bar t$. The constant-module tensor/stalk comparison identifies this stalk complex with $K_{\bar t}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M[0]$. Hence its cohomology vanishes outside $[a,b]$, for every $M$ and $\bar t$.

proof.text: Conversely assume the stated condition for all geometric points and all ordinary $A$-modules. Let $\mathcal F$ be any $A_T$-module sheaf, placed in degree zero, and fix $i\notin[a,b]$. The unbounded derived tensor/stalk comparison gives $(K\otimes_{A_T}^{\mathbf L}\mathcal F[0])_{\bar t}\cong K_{\bar t}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\mathcal F_{\bar t}[0]$. Its right-hand side has zero $i$-th cohomology by the assumption with $M=\mathcal F_{\bar t}$. Step 1 therefore gives zero for every stalk of $H^i(K\otimes_{A_T}^{\mathbf L}\mathcal F[0])$. Geometric-stalk conservativity applied to its underlying abelian sheaf makes this cohomology sheaf zero. Since $\mathcal F$ and $i$ were arbitrary, this is precisely Tor amplitude $[a,b]$.

Let $u:U\to T$ be any scheme morphism and suppose $K$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$. The constant-coefficient module inverse image is exact, agrees with inverse image on underlying abelian sheaves, and identifies $u^{-1}A_T$ with $A_U$. Thus $u^*K$ is represented by applying $u^*$ termwise. For a geometric point $\bar v$ of $U$, the natural inverse-image stalk comparison gives $(u^*C^n)_{\bar v}\cong C^n_{u\circ\bar v}$ in every degree. These are additive and $A$-linear: the canonical comparison respects products and addition, and its naturality for each scalar-multiplication map $m_c:C^n\to C^n$ gives $c\,x\mapsto c\,x$ for all $c\in A$. Naturality for $d^n$ makes them an isomorphism of complexes. By exactness of stalks it induces $(u^*K)_{\bar v}\cong K_{u\circ\bar v}$ in $D(A)$. Step 2 says that this complex tensored with any $A$-module has cohomology in $[a,b]$. Applying step 3 on $U$ proves that $u^*K$ has the same Tor interval.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q66-0a6dd2655 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and every cited statement in full. Item: a geometric-stalk test for Tor amplitude on the small étale site, for any commutative A and any scheme T, plus the consequence that u^* preserves Tor intervals. The statement is unchanged, adds no hypothesis, and matches Stacks 0DJJ (sites-cohomology lemma-tor-amplitude-stalk) on the ordinary étale coefficient category that the parent sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation uses in steps 3 and 4. Geometric points use algebraically closed Ω throughout (def-weil-geometric-point), the same as in the cited tensor nodes. Step 1: stalk exactness on Ab plus the exact-functor homology lemma give H^i(E)_t̄ ≅ H^i(E_t̄) for unbounded E, and conservativity detects zero; the module-to-abelian forgetful step is written out. Step 2: the definition tested on the constant sheaf M_T[0], then step 1, then lem-sfb-geometric-stalk-tensor-constant-single, for arbitrary M. Step 3: lem-sfb-etale-derived-tensor-stalk (unbounded, any K and L) with L = F[0] and M = F_t̄, then step 1 and conservativity; this follows the converse argument of 0DJJ. Step 4: prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact (1)-(3) and the stalk pullback lemma (03Q1 (3)), with A-linearity and the differentials handled by naturality, give (u^*K)_v̄ ≅ K_{u∘v̄}; then step 2 on T and step 3 on U. The delivery creates no new nodes. Duplicate search over all statement nodes: lem-sfb-tor-interval-local-detection is pro-étale cover/open-closed locality, and the pc Tor nodes are Zariski, so neither is a duplicate. There is no cycle and no SGA. Tags 0DJJ, 0DEN, 03Q1, 03PT, 03PU and 010N were verified against the tags file. I accept all five tool_uses: the two genuinely off-route ones are the generic tensor/stalk comparisons (sk-lem-integral-models, sk-prop-ctf-finite-proper), and the other three are on the unit's route anyway. Edge cases checked: empty T, K = 0, K = A_T[0], a = b, unbounded K, non-Noetherian A, arbitrary u. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem geometricStalk_torAmplitude_test (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] (T : Scheme.{u}) (K : DerivedCategoryModule A T) (a b : ℤ) (_hab : a ≤ b) : (DerivedCategory.hasTorAmplitudeIn A T a b K ↔ ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ T) (M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) (i : ℤ), i < a ∨ b < i → IsZero ((_root_.DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) i).obj (((pointSmallEtale t).sheafFiber (A := ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K ⊗ (_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) 0).obj M))) ∧ (∀ (U : Scheme.{u}) (f : U ⟶ T), DerivedCategory.hasTorAmplitudeIn A T a b K → DerivedCategory.hasTorAmplitudeIn A U a b ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f).mapDerivedCategory.obj K))

Ring any commutative A (Type u+1), no extra hypotheses; K an unbounded DerivedCategoryModule; a ≤ b kept; the iff ranges over all geometric points (Ω : Type u, algebraically closed) and all modules (ModuleCat.{u+1} A); i < a ∨ b < i → IsZero(H^i(stalk K ⊗ M[0])), where ⊗ is the derived monoidal structure on D(ModuleCat A) (checked by #synth); the pullback conjunct holds for arbitrary f with the same interval, via upperStar.mapDerivedCategory, which is the framework's own D((f)^*[A]).
